summary: Playbook: reconcile conflicting routing templates during SLA template imports
summary_long: When teams import bulk SLA/routing templates (CSV/JSON) via the support tooling, we occasionally see template priority inversion where older, lower-priority templates shadow recently applied higher-priority rules. This ticket holds an operational playbook to detect, reconcile, and safely roll back conflicting template imports and to automate safe re-apply logic.
description: Issue summary: Multiple template imports in the last 48h resulted in routing templates being applied out-of-order; highest-priority SLAs are not taking effect for some support paths. Impact: customers on internal testing and dedicated tiers receiving incorrect routing to tier-1 rather than tier-2. Scope: affects support-routing config store and template import tool. Goal: provide a reproducible playbook for detection, fast mitigation, and durable remediation, plus a short automation to validate imports before apply.
impact: Routing misclassification for ~12 support queues and degraded SLA enforcement for internal escalations. No customer-facing incidents reported yet, but internal SLA alerts suppressed incorrectly.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In staging, import templates batch 'sla_batch_2026-02-17.json' via support-tools import API
2) Run 'supportctl export-templates --since 2026-02-15' to view applied priority ordering
3) Observe that template IDs with later timestamps have lower effective priority in the routing-engine
4) Query routing decisions for sample routes using 'routing-inspect --queue support-ops --time 2026-02-19T10:00Z'
5) Verify mismatches against expected ordering in Confluence spec
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: import process assigns stable numeric 'order' based on DB insert id rather than declared priority field
Checked support-tool logs (s3://support-logs/imports/2026-02-17); observed import worker reordered items when concurrent imports happened
Routing-engine reads 'priority_weight' from templates but a migration last quarter added 'priority_epoch' which is not present in older templates; epoch default = 0 caused older templates to win
Telemetry: between 2026-02-17 00:00 and 2026-02-19 12:00, 18 routing decisions for internal queues referenced templates with epoch=0 despite newer templates having explicit epoch=2
Related: INT-46290 shows an unrelated restore failure — potential concurrent restore was running during import
Confirmed no schema change pushed to production in the same window except a support-tools hotfix (PR 3987) which adjusted import concurrency limits
detection_queries: Elastic: count by template_epoch where effective_routing_mismatch=true and environment=prod-us-east
Support DB: select template_id, priority_epoch, inserted_at from routing_templates order by inserted_at desc limit 200
mitigation_plan: 1) Put support-tooling import endpoint into readonly mode: supportctl set-import-mode readonly --reason 'template merge investigation'
2) Run a targeted re-evaluate for affected queues: supportctl reevaluate-queues --queues 'internal-escalations,platform-sre,dev-tools'
3) If re-evaluate isn't sufficient, rollback last import batch via supportctl import-rollback --batch sla_batch_2026-02-17
4) Short-term: apply a forced priority patch to routing-engine for affected queues (route_priority_override) until templates are reconciled
5) Notify #support-ops and #sre with status and timeframe
rollback_steps: 1) Identify import batch id from support-logs (path in investigation_notes)
3) monitor routing decision rate and SLA alerts for 30 minutes
4) if alerts resume, escalate to oncall routing-engine lead
automation_tasks: Add preflight validator to support-tools: validate presence of 'priority_epoch' and consistent 'priority_weight' ordering in batch
Implement optimistic-apply with dry-run: supportctl import --dry-run returns diff and ordering report
Add unit/integration test that simulates concurrent imports and asserts stable ordering
Create daily audit job to detect epoch=0 templates with recent inserted_at > 2026-01-01
